A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same batching study. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original batching and training-time experiments, recompilation measurements, and test-RMSE curves for SchNet and MPEU on QM9 and AFLOW.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds PaiNN timing experiments and statistical comparisons of final test RMSE.

M1.justification: The static and dynamic batching procedures, padding variants, and Algorithms 1–5 retain their substantive steps. PaiNN is an additional model used to evaluate batching, not a modification of the batching method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate QM9 molecular internal energy and AFLOW crystal enthalpy using the same graph construction. The removed node-level discussion described possible applications, not an evaluated task.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain dynamic, static-2^N, and static-64 batching. Static-constant retains the same comparison subset in Appendix F and Table 1. PaiNN extends the evaluated model configurations rather than adding a batching comparator.

E3.justification: v2 extends the experimental design with the equivariant PaiNN model across both datasets and all four batch sizes. Existing hardware, two-million-step GPU experiments, shorter CPU experiments, and timing measurements are retained; the principal change is the substantial model-configuration extension.

E4.justification: The learning comparison gains an analysis of final-RMSE distributions through pairwise tests and heatmaps in Appendix H. Existing padding-distribution, recompilation, training-duration, CPU, and static-constant analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 primarily compares averaged learning curves; v2 introduces pairwise Student t-tests, t-statistics, p-values, and interpretation thresholds of 0.05 and 0.10. This substantially changes the inferential reporting. The stated ten repetitions are retained, without a reported increase in runs.

E6.justification: New PaiNN results show dynamic batching fastest on AFLOW and roughly matching static-64 on QM9, with over 2.7× speedup over static-2^N at QM9 batch size 128 (Figures 4–5). Recompilation bars also change between v1 Figure 4 and v2 Figure 6. New statistical results contain an inconsistency: Figure 17 assigns p = 0.033 to dynamic versus static-64, whereas Section 8 attributes it to static-2^N.

T1.justification: Section 7 adds mathematical definitions of PaiNN's scalar and equivariant representations and their update rules in Equations 8–9. Existing batching formalization and Equations 1–7 remain substantively unchanged; no new proof or theoretical guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 removes v1's claim that a static variant is fastest after convergence, replaces the 33% speedup headline with 2.7×, and explicitly includes hardware dependence. It also replaces the blanket absence of learning differences with a claim of significant differences for selected configurations.

C2.justification: v2 explains PaiNN's dynamic-batching advantage through greater gradient-update costs and attributes learning differences to fewer real graphs per batch, while suggesting Adam may explain remaining agreement. It removes v1 Appendix G's substantive node-level applicability discussion. Appendix E nevertheless retains the earlier assertion of no significant learning differences.

D1.justification: v2 documents PaiNN's 177,568 parameters and newly mentions using Adam, without establishing an optimizer change. The Software and Data section changes the repository address and adds access instructions for additional t-test heatmaps. Hardware and timing instrumentation remain documented as before.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting PaiNN and its use, speedup terminology, and statistical testing: Schütt et al. (2021), Kubečka et al. (2024), Hennessy and Patterson (2011), Hartmann et al. (2023), and Ross (2017). The related-work section and central novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much of the prose are retained. Revisions concentrate on the abstract, contribution bullets, model descriptions, results, and discussion. The node-level appendix is removed, the training-duration appendix moves from H to G, and a new statistical Appendix H is added.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with PaiNN timing panels, a speedup bar chart, and separate t-statistic and p-value heatmaps. The recompilation chart is redrawn with changed proportions, colors, and labeling. Most earlier plots and Table 1 are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The PaiNN experiments provide a concrete counterexample to v1's static-winner conclusion, strengthening practical batching recommendations. The quality gain is limited by the new statistical section's comparator mismatch between Section 8 and Figure 17, Appendix E's contradictory retained learning claim, and removal of the node-level applicability discussion.
